explanation: Working in Java, he saw that chickens fed polished rice developed a similar illness, while those fed whole rice did not. The missing nutrient was vitamin B1, thiamine.

claims.text: Christiaan Eijkman shared the 1929 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work showing that beriberi was linked to a diet of polished white rice.
Beriberi was not linked to diets of raw fish, cassava or maize.
Eijkman worked in Java, in the Dutch East Indies.
Chickens fed polished rice developed a beriberi-like illness, while chickens fed unpolished rice did not.
Beriberi is caused by a lack of thiamine, vitamin B1.
